newsitem.title: USA: US Senators to propose bill to raise cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: US Senators to propose bill to raise cigarette tax.

text.p: Two U.S. senators said Tuesday they would introduce legislation to raise the tax on cigarettes by 43 cents a pack to pay for child health care.

Sen. Orrin Hatch, a Republican from Utah, and Sen. Edward Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat, said they were sponsoring legislation that would raise the cigarette tax to 67 cents per pack from the current 24 cents.

The tax increase would raise about $30 billion over five years, Kennedy said. Two-thirds of the money raised by the cigarette tax increase would go toward the children's health insurance program, while one-third would go toward reducing the deficit, the senators said.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, however, said he opposed the measure.

"We don't think another tax increase and another big government takeover of a problem in America is the way to go," the Mississippi Republican said. "I feel very strongly against the Kennedy approach," he said.
